summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft has reached a historic milestone by successfully communicating with mission controllers from a distance of one light-day from Earth. In civil space activities, NASA announced a Mid-Power Electric Rocket Challenge for U.S. companies, conducted a new RS-25 engine test in support of future Artemis lunar missions, and scheduled the end of science operations for its Terra satellite on Dec. 1. Deep-space research achieved notable progress as the James Webb Space Telescope confirmed a first-of-its-kind star merger, the European Space Agency's Hera probe inspected NASA’s previous asteroid crash site, and researchers utilized NASA data to deploy a new cryptography-inspired search method for elusive pulsars. Internationally, China rolled out a launch vehicle to transport the first foreign astronaut to the Tiangong space station, Poland’s Ministry of Defense announced plans to acquire new satellites to expand its space capabilities, and engine trouble forced Japan’s Hayabusa2 probe to cancel a planned asteroid landing. In defense and military space news, the U.S. Air Force conducted a test launch of a Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile, European defense firms MBDA and Atmos partnered to study space-based strike weapons, and a recent United Launch Alliance launch failure created operational complications for the Space Force. Commercial space developments saw non-profit Common Space announce plans to launch a humanitarian satellite in 2027, while Sophia Space successfully tested orbital-compute software on the active Kepler constellation. Looking ahead, space monitoring efforts turn to NASA’s upcoming coverage and prelaunch preparations for the Northrop Grumman CRS-25 resupply mission.
